raw.abstractText: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) represent the first line of host immune defense against a broad spectrum of microorganisms. Whether naturally occurring or synthetically designed, these small peptides can potently inhibit microbial growth and remain stable under diverse conditions. Most AMPs act by directly disrupting fungal or bacterial membranes. In this study, we identified a glycine-rich peptide with strong antifungal activity against Botrytis cinerea. We further investigated its mode of action (MOA) and demonstrated its preventive antifungal activity in plants. Our work focuses primarily on the in vitro characterization of AMP features in the context of plant-Botrytis interactions.

raw.abstractText: Virus-induced gene silencing (VIGS) is a powerful reverse genetics tool that enables the transient knockdown of gene expression in plants by exploiting their natural antiviral defense mechanisms. This chapter presents a detailed protocol for applying a Cowpea severe mosaic virus (CPSMV)-based VIGS system to study gene function in soybean (Glycine max), with a focus on symbiotic root nodulation. VIGS allows systemic silencing of target genes, making it especially valuable to study pathways involving systemic signaling. The protocol includes Agrobacterium-mediated propagation of CPSMV variants in Nicotiana benthamiana, followed by mechanical inoculation of soybean plants and nodulation analysis. Detailed steps for vector construction, viral amplification, plant infection, and downstream molecular and phenotypic analyses are provided. This protocol is reproducible, accessible, and suitable for functional genomics studies in soybean, particularly for genes involved in nodulation but also in other developmental or stress-related processes.

raw.abstractText:
Objective

To evaluate metabolic outcomes in women with and without Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS, formerly Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS))) receiving multidisciplinary care through a women's health telehealth platform that combines physician and registered dietitian support.

Methods

Retrospective cohort analysis of 919 women with BMI ≥ 25 initiating care in 2024, with ≥ 6 months follow-up (mean 9.6 months). Participants included 557 with PMOS and 362 without. Outcomes extracted from the electronic health record (EHR) included change in weight, HbA1c, HOMA-IR, fasting insulin, fasting glucose, ALT, AST and total cholesterol between baseline and last measured value. Linear regression models adjusted for baseline values of each outcome, age, BMI, race/ethnicity and follow-up time.

Results

Significant improvements were observed across all metabolic markers for the group overall: HOMA-IR (-14.0%), fasting insulin (-15.6%), fasting glucose (-13.0%), HbA1c (-6.2%), ALT (-21.2%), AST (-25.5%), total cholesterol (-8.0%) and weight (-4.9%). PCOS status was not associated with differential improvement in any outcome after adjustment. GLP-1 receptor agonist use was associated with greater weight loss; however, improvements were also observed in the no-medication group.

Conclusions

Women with PCOS achieved metabolic improvements equivalent to those without PMOS through a multidisciplinary telehealth model despite presenting with a more adverse metabolic profile at baseline.

raw.abstractText: This study aimed to explore the processing mechanism of single medicinal herbs in compound prescriptions, compare the pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic changes of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula before and after processing, and elucidate its underlying mechanism against gastric ulcers. The results showed that six components, namely, corydaline, coptisine chloride, palmatine, berberine chloride, phellopterin, and imperatorin, exerted anti-ulcer activities. The optimal vinegar-processing parameters for Corydalis yanhusuo were determined as follows: processing temperature of 84°C, vinegar dosage of 37%, and baking time of 35 min. Vinegar-processed Corydalis yanhusuo could accelerate the in vivo distribution of alkaloid components in the formula, elevate the plasma concentration, and prolong the in vivo retention time of coumarin components. The synergistic effects of the two types of active ingredients endow the vinegar-processed Yuanhu Zhitong Formula with significantly superior antigastric ulcer activity compared with the raw formula. Moreover, network pharmacology results revealed that this formula exerts therapeutic effects against gastric ulcers mainly by regulating the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. This study clarified the optimal processing technology and the pharmacodynamic material basis of Yuanhu Zhitong Formula against gastric ulcers, confirmed the efficacy-enhancing effect of processing, and provided data support for the formulation of its processing production standards and clinical medication.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Caffeine is consumed for its presumed cognitive benefits, yet controlled studies have repeatedly failed to find effects on inhibitory control. Cross-sectional work suggests that people with elevated attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms may benefit from chronic, moderate caffeine consumption, but whether acute intake improves cognition in proportion to symptom severity has not been tested experimentally.

Aims

We tested whether 250 mg of caffeine improves active inhibition (withholding a prepared response) and reactive inhibition (resolving response conflict), and whether ADHD symptom severity moderates these effects.

Methods

In a preregistered, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial, a nonclinical sample of 36 young adults received 250 mg of caffeine or placebo in counterbalanced order, with testing 45 min after ingestion. Active inhibition was assessed with a Go/No-Go task (204 trials), reactive inhibition with an arrow flanker task (200 trials) and symptoms with the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale. Mixed-effects models included treatment, symptom severity, their interaction and ten covariates; Bayes factors quantified evidence for the null.

Results

Both tasks produced their benchmark effects (dz = 1.24 and 1.09) and all indices were reliable (split-half r = 0.73-0.98). Caffeine affected neither commission errors (BF01 = 4.98), response criterion (5.14), Go reaction time (2.83), reaction time variability (4.35), flanker reaction time (5.49) nor flanker accuracy (5.09). ADHD symptoms moderated no effect (15 preregistered tests; smallest p = 0.514), yet predicted performance itself (flanker accuracy r = -0.42), indicating that the null is not due to an insensitive measure.

Conclusions

Caffeine produced no acute benefit for either form of inhibition, and ADHD symptoms did not moderate its effects. Bayes factors supported the absence rather than the nondetection of these effects, arguing against an acute improvement of inhibitory control that scales with ADHD symptom severity in nonclinical young adults. Whether this also holds for chronic consumption or for adults with diagnosed ADHD remains to be tested.

raw.abstractText: The collagen triple helix is the most abundant protein structural motif in animals. It tolerates any amino acid in its Xaa and Yaa positions but demands glycine (Gly) at every third position, where the residue packs into the sterically forbidding core of the triple helix and donates the recurring interstrand N-H⋯OC hydrogen bond that stitches the three strands together. (2S)-Proline (Pro) and (2S,4R)-4-hydroxyproline (Hyp) are enriched far above their proteome-wide abundance because they preorganize individual strands into the polyproline II conformation, lowering the entropic cost of folding. We asked whether the triple helix is intrinsically stable enough to form from strands that carry no such preorganization, that is, from polyglycine. To offset the conformational entropy of a Gly-rich tract, we embedded Gly<sub>6</sub> within flanking triple-helical (Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>n</sub> clamps in Ac-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>6</sub>-Gly<sub>6</sub>-(Pro-Hyp-Gly)<sub>5</sub>-Pro-Hyp-NH<sub>2</sub> and compared it with an otherwise identical peptide in which Gly<sub>6</sub> was replaced by two [2-(2-aminoethoxy)ethoxy]acetic acid units, a flexible, length-matched spacer that lacks most of the regularly spaced backbone amides of Gly<sub>6</sub>. Circular dichroism spectroscopy revealed the diagnostic positive band at 225 nm. The molar ellipticity of the spacer-containing control was 86% of that of the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, matching the 35/41 = 85% ratio of residues capable of triple-helix formation and consistent with the Gly<sub>6</sub> segment contributing to the triple-helical signal. Thermal denaturation yielded a T<sub>m</sub> of 46.8°C for the Gly<sub>6</sub>-containing peptide, 6.3°C higher than that of the matched spacer control. This added stability indicates that the polyglycine tract is not merely accommodated within the helix but contributes stabilizing interstrand hydrogen bonds. Together, these data indicate that three polyglycine strands can form a collagen triple helix when flanked by triple-helical clamps. This result is consistent with the idea that the triple-helical architecture predates the recruitment of Pro and Hyp, informs the evolutionary origin of collagen, and offers a blunt-ended, symmetric scaffold for designing peptidic triple helices.

raw.abstractText:
While insulin activates the sympathetic nervous system in experimental settings, whether therapeutic insulin administration is associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance under free-living conditions remains unclear. This prospective observational study investigated the association between insulin dosing and cardiac autonomic balance in adults with type 1 diabetes managed exclusively with insulin therapy. Participants underwent continuous heart rate variability (HRV) and glucose monitoring over 4 consecutive days during routine daily activities. Cardiac sympathetic predominance was assessed using the low-frequency power to high-frequency power (LF/HF) ratio derived from HRV analysis, and associations were evaluated using generalized estimating equations. A higher last bolus insulin dose was associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the early sleep phase. A higher basal insulin dose was also associated with an increased LF/HF ratio during the late sleep phase. These associations persisted after adjustment for mean glucose and mean absolute glucose change during the corresponding sleep phases. Under free-living conditions, higher insulin doses were associated with dose-dependent increases in cardiac sympathetic predominance, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing may be linked to cardiac autonomic regulation in individuals with type 1 diabetes, highlighting the importance of considering cardiac autonomic balance and potential cardiovascular risk when optimizing insulin therapy.

Article highlights

The relationship between therapeutic insulin administration and cardiac autonomic balance under free-living conditions remains unclear. We examined whether insulin dosing was associated with cardiac sympathetic predominance during daily life in adults with type 1 diabetes managed with insulin therapy. Higher last bolus and basal insulin doses were associated with increased cardiac sympathetic predominance during the early and late sleep phases, respectively, independent of glycemic profiles. These findings suggest that insulin dosing patterns may be linked to cardiac autonomic balance, with potential implications for optimizing insulin therapy in type 1 diabetes.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Prolonged exposure to hepatotoxic antiretroviral therapy (ART) could lead to chronic liver injury, which might increase risk of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). We used causal inference methods to evaluate if cumulative exposure to ART with known mechanisms of chronic liver injury is associated with HCC among people with HIV (PWH), by chronic liver disease (CLD) status.

Methods

We conducted a cohort study of antiretroviral-naive PWH with and without diagnosed CLD who initiated ART in the Veterans Affairs between 1999 and 2023. Exposure to ART with known mechanism of chronic liver injury (mitochondrial toxicity or accumulation of toxic intermediates) was determined monthly through prescription fills. Incident HCC was identified by Veterans Affairs National Cancer Registry and/or recorded diagnoses. Marginal structural models estimated odds ratios (ORs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) of HCC associated with cumulative exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART compared with ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms, by CLD status.

Results

Among 11,854 PWH without CLD and 6771 PWH with CLD, we observed 112 and 378 HCC events, respectively. Among PWH without CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was associated with HCC when compared with ≥4 years of use of ART without chronic liver injury mechanisms (OR = 4.02 [95% CI: 1.00-16.24]). Among PWH with CLD, ≥4 years of exposure to chronic liver injury-inducing ART was not associated with HCC (OR = 1.36; 95% CI: 0.68-2.72).

Conclusion

Four or more years of ART with a chronic liver injury mechanism was associated with HCC among PWH without CLD, but not those with CLD.

raw.abstractText: Hepatitis A virus (HAV) infection is an uncommon indication for liver transplantation, and donor-derived or transfusion-associated HAV infection is rare. Data describing HAV recurrence or early acquisition following liver transplantation, particularly with longitudinal quantitative viral kinetics, are limited. We describe two liver transplant recipients with graft HAV infection occurring in different immunological contexts. One patient underwent emergency liver transplantation for HAV-related acute liver failure and subsequently developed recurrent HAV infection of the graft. The second patient underwent liver transplantation for paracetamol-induced acute liver failure and acquired HAV infection following peri-operative blood transfusion in the early post-transplant period. Serial qualitative and retrospective quantitative HAV ribonucleic acid (RNA) polymerase chain reaction (PCR) measurements were analysed alongside biochemical and clinical parameters. In the patient transplanted for fulminant HAV infection, serum HAV RNA declined rapidly after transplantation, consistent with removal of the infected native liver, followed by recurrent viraemia associated with graft hepatitis during the second and third post-transplant months, and with viral clearance by 4 months. In contrast, the transfusion-acquired HAV infection occurred in the setting of profound immunosuppression and absence of pre-existing immunity, resulting in a higher peak viral load, prolonged viraemia lasting over 9 months, and more severe graft hepatitis. Viral doubling times during viraemic expansion were similar in both cases but sustained high-level viraemia was observed only in the de novo infection. These cases provide novel insights into HAV viral kinetics following liver transplantation and highlight important differences between recurrent infection and newly acquired HAV infection in immunosuppressed recipients.

raw.abstractText: Melatonin (MEL) is an endogenous hormone that regulates circadian rhythm, immune function and oxidative stress responses. Norepinephrine (NE), an endogenous catecholamine, increases blood pressure through the sympathetic nervous system and is commonly administered intraoperatively or in the clinically ill patient for hemodynamic support. Although endogenous NE is known to stimulate MEL synthesis, the effects of exogenous intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentration, particularly under general anaesthesia (GA), remain poorly characterised. This study examined the influence of intravenous NE on plasma MEL concentrations in healthy volunteers, both awake and under general anaesthesia. A secondary analysis was conducted using data from a prospective, single-centre, cross-over study involving volunteers who received stepwise NE infusions while awake and under total intravenous general anaesthesia. Arterial blood samples were collected to determine plasma MEL and NE concentrations. Linear mixed-effects modelling was used to assess the relationship between NE and MEL concentrations. A total of 36 healthy volunteers were enroled, yielding 417 MEL-NE samples. Intravenous NE administration was significantly associated with higher plasma MEL concentration, corresponding to an estimated 26% increase in MEL per 1 standard-deviation increase in NE concentration (Estimate = 0.230, p < 0.001). MEL concentrations were approximately 43% higher in the awake phase compared to GA (Estimate = 0.356, p < 0.001). GA did not significantly modify the NE-MEL association (Estimate = -0.02877, p = 0.528). Substantial positive correlation was observed between baseline MEL concentrations and the magnitude of the response to NE administration (r = 0.74). In conclusion, intravenous NE increases plasma MEL concentrations in both awake and anaesthetised individuals. Substantial interindividual variation in MEL response suggests underlying physiological differences. Future studies should explore the long-term effects of NE administration on MEL concentrations. Objective

To compare serum total tau and α-synuclein among controls, drug-naïve children with attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and children with ADHD receiving methylphenidate.

Methods

Original ELISA spreadsheets provided 26 controls, 29 evaluable drug-naïve participants and 32 methylphenidate-treated participants. Boundary-coded results (> 500 pg/mL for tau; < 938 pg/mL for α-synuclein) were assigned the recorded boundary for rank-based analyses. Groups were compared using Kruskal-Wallis tests and Dunn-Bonferroni contrasts; within-group associations used Spearman correlations.

Results

α-Synuclein differed among groups (H = 49.859, p < 0.001, ε2 = 0.570), with all pairwise contrasts significant. Tau also differed (H = 10.492, p = 0.005, ε2 = 0.101); drug-naïve ADHD had lower tau than controls, whereas the treated group differed from neither comparator after correction. The α-synuclein-tau correlation remained significant after false-discovery-rate adjustment only in drug-naïve ADHD (ρ = 0.443, adjusted p = 0.048).

Conclusions

Serum α-synuclein and total tau showed distinct cross-sectional group patterns. These associations do not establish methylphenidate effects and require prospective confirmation.

raw.abstractText: TYRO3, AXL, and MERTK, the TAM receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs), play roles in phagocytosis and negative regulation of immune responses, contributing to homeostasis in many adult tissues. Aberrant TAM signaling leads to diseases including autoimmune disorders, viral infection, inflammation, and cancer. Development of successful drugs targeting TAM receptors is hindered by incomplete knowledge of the receptor activation mechanism. Receptor dimerization is assumed to play a role, as seen for most RTKs. However, full biological responses require the TAM ligands to engage phosphatidylserine in an opposing cell or virus membrane, suggesting a more complex mechanism, possibly involving higher-order receptor oligomerization or clustering. Here, we present an X-ray crystal structure of the ectodomain of MERTK, which adopts a highly curved conformation with key interdomain boundaries stabilized by N-linked glycan moieties. We show that this MERTK extracellular region (ECR) forms a similar conformation in solution using small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), which also suggests a flexible ECR. We compare these crystallographic and solution data for MERTK with SAXS and AlphaFold structural predictions for the other two TAM receptors. SAXS data confirm that each TAM ECR has a distinct curvature, with TYRO3 the most bent and AXL relatively straight. This leads us to speculate that these different ectodomain conformations guide receptor-specific functions. The MERTK X-ray crystal structure also suggests a head-to-tail intermolecular interaction between the Ig2 domain of one MERTK and the FNIIIb domain of a second that has intriguing parallels with interactions that have been proposed to regulate Eph receptor clustering.

raw.abstractText: Activity-guided separation of medicinal plants requires linking activity signals and chromatographic resolution in complex matrices. In this study, based on a previously established HPLC-DPPH platform, medium-pressure prefractionation and preparative chromatographic purification were applied for the targeted isolation of free radical scavengers from Saxifraga tangutica (S. tangutica). Medium-pressure prefractionation reduced sample complexity and enriched active fractions, while Click XION chromatography concentrated the target fraction. Subsequent purification on the ReproSil-Pur C18 AQ column resolved this fraction into two baseline-separated active peaks, affording compounds with purities greater than 95%. The isolated compounds were identified as quercetin-3-O-β-D-glucoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside and quercetin-3-O-β-D-galactoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside, a pair of C-4″-epimeric quercetin 3,7-di-O-glycosides. Both compounds exhibited DPPH radical-scavenging activity, with IC<sub>50</sub> values of 68.94 ± 2.77 and 75.59 ± 2.14 μM, respectively. DFT calculations, molecular docking, and ADMET prediction further supported the comparative interpretation of their electronic features, antioxidant-related interaction potential, and predicted pharmacokinetic profiles. Overall, this study achieved the activity guided isolation and activity evaluation of a pair of high-purity C-4″-epimeric flavonol diglycosides from S. tangutica, providing a practical chromatographic strategy for the targeted characterization of structurally similar bioactive constituents from medicinal plants.

raw.abstractText: Ripened washed-rind and long-ripened cheeses owe their prized sulfurous, savory character to intensive proteolysis and amino-acid catabolism; the same activity, when poorly controlled, also generates sensory off-flavors and toxic biogenic amines (BAs). Histamine and tyramine reach up to approximately 2000-2500 and 1000-2000 mg/kg in extreme samples, although most cheeses contain far less, so that a 30-g portion of a high-histamine cheese can exceed the 50-mg per-meal intake regarded as without adverse effect in healthy adults. Flavor formation and chemical safety have traditionally been studied apart. This critical review reframes them as two outcomes of one metabolism: Proteolysis liberates a shared free amino-acid pool from which volatile sulfur compounds (VSCs) and BAs arise. Because the principal VSCs derive from methionine whereas the major BAs derive from histidine, tyrosine, ornithine, arginine, and lysine, we treat the branches not as direct competitors for one substrate but as metabolically coupled fates linked by shared proteolytic supply, overlapping physicochemical controls and microbial cross-feeding. Integrating evidence across cheese families, we reclassify the ripening microbiota into condition-dependent functional guilds, formalize metabolic bivalence (organisms that both generate flavor and degrade amines), and define a sensory inflection point separating the windowed VSC dose-response from the monotonic BA hazard. We critically appraise multi-omics, volatilomics, biosensors, machine learning, and digital twins, and outline a precision-fermentation roadmap. Current, largely in vitro, and single-variety evidence is consistent with, but does not establish, controllable decoupling, which we frame as a testable hypothesis that recasts cheese quality as a controllable metabolic-allocation problem.

raw.abstractText: Prosthetic heart valve development consists of several branching, innovative strategies to mediate the complex native environment that wears down valve durability. Anti-calcification treatments are being applied to pericardial tissue, durable polymers are being developed that mitigate oxidative degradation and stress cracking, and heart valve tissue engineering has introduced resorbable scaffolds that can develop into stable, functional tissue. In each case, an increasing breadth of strategies is being developed to curb the persistent issue of valve deterioration. This study aimed to synthesize and characterize an ascorbic acid-containing polyurethane to impart antioxidant properties to degradable scaffolds for tissue engineered heart valve (TEHV) replacement. Blends of poly(carbonate-ascorbic acid) urethane (PCAU) and poly(carbonate urethane) urea (PCUU) were fabricated into microporous scaffolds to evaluate the impact of PCAU in vitro on mechanics, degradation, cell viability, calcification, bacterial adhesion, and in vivo on native tissue response in a juvenile rat subcutaneous model. PCAU blended with PCUU in a 25:75 ratio (PCAU-25) had mechanical properties similar to PCUU, while higher concentrations of PCAU were not mechanically robust. PCAU-25 showed greater reactive oxygen species (ROS) inhibition and degradation, and reduced calcification and bacterial adhesion in vitro. In a juvenile rat subcutaneous model, both PCUU and PCAU-25 groups showed negligible calcification after 4 weeks. PCAU-25, however, showed much greater cell infiltration and immune response, possibly due to an accelerated rate of degradation. PCAU-25 was then fabricated into a polymeric valve scaffold and underwent basic mechanical and hydrodynamic performance assessment that demonstrated function similar to PCUU valves previously reported. These findings demonstrate proof-of-concept for a new polyurethane formulation incorporating ascorbic acid for antioxidant bioactivity and translatability into a functional TEHV scaffold.

raw.abstractText: Vitamin D is a nutrient and prohormone obtained from diet and supplements and synthesized in the skin. It is essential for calcium and phosphate homeostasis and skeletal health and influences multiple extra-skeletal processes, yet deficiency remains common worldwide. This narrative review summarizes vitamin D sources, physiology, metabolism, pharmacokinetics, clinical relevance and safety and outlines the distinct pharmacokinetic profiles and clinical roles of vitamin D, calcidiol and calcitriol and its analogues. Evidence consistently supports vitamin D, combined with calcium, for preventing and treating deficiency-related skeletal disorders in high-risk populations, and in specific conditions such as malabsorption, chronic kidney disease, hypoparathyroidism and frailty. In vitamin D-replete populations, large trials show limited extra-skeletal benefits, apart from modest effects on cancer mortality and progression from prediabetes to Type 2 diabetes. Untargeted screening is not recommended. Future research should prioritize targeted supplementation, standardized assays and identification of populations most likely to benefit from supplementation.

raw.abstractText:
Background

The results of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) regarding the effect of vitamin D supplementation on mortality reduction are conflicting.

Objective

The aim of this study was to assess the level of evidence through a sensitivity analysis of the meta-analysis by Shah et al. (2024) using the Rebuilt the Evidence Base (REB) method.

Methods

The main inclusion criterion was a double-blind, placebo-controlled RCT design. The exclusion criteria were trials combining vitamin D with other nutrients and unpublished RCTs. The main outcome was all-cause mortality. A bias analysis was performed, followed by a hypothetico-deductive analysis to determine the confirmatory or exploratory nature of each RCT. The REB method was used to interpret the results and assess the level of evidence.

Results

Among the 25 RCTs included in the meta-analysis by Shah et al., the analysis was performed on 8 RCTs at low risk of bias including 30 320 participants. Seven RCTs raised some concerns, and two RCTs were at high risk of bias according to ROB2. Bias arose from the randomization process, deviations from intended interventions, missing outcome data, and selection of the reported results. The results were statistically significant, in favor of vitamin D supplementation: RR = 0.96 (95% CI [0.92, 1.00]), p = 0.04. No RCT was conclusive.

Conclusion

According to the REB method, there is an evidence signal regarding the benefit of vitamin D supplementation in the population aged 75 and older, which remains to be confirmed.

raw.authorString: Salikhova D, Maksimov Y, Nebogatikov V, Belousova E, Orlova E, Globa A, Lapshina M, Ustyugov A, Goldshtein D.
raw.abstractText: Background Cell therapy is a promising approach for treating neurological disorders, but its safety remains a major concern, including the origin of cells, cultivation methods, and route of administration. Repeated systemic delivery is often required for long-term studies, yet the safety of chronic retro-orbital administration of human glial progenitor cells (GPCs) has not been characterised. This pilot study evaluated the potential risks and pathological processes associated with chronic retro-orbital administration of human iPSC-derived GPCs in mice. Methods GPCs were derived from human induced pluripotent stem cells and injected into the retro-orbital venous sinus of male C57Bl/6 J mice under isoflurane anaesthesia. Two pilot experiments were performed: a high-dose experiment with 500 × 10  3 (n = 9), 150 × 10  3 (n = 5), and 50 × 10  3 (n = 5) cells/mouse administered weekly for two months, and a control group (n = 9) receiving dPBS. Locomotor and exploratory activity were assessed in the open field test. Blood biochemical markers (ALT, AST, AST/ALT ratio, LDH, GGT, and total bilirubin) were measured, and brain sections were analysed by H&E staining and immunohistochemistry for glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP). Statistical analysis was performed using ANOVA on ranks with Dunn’s post-hoc test or one-way ANOVA with Holm–Sidak correction. Results Chronic administration of the high dose (500 × 10  3 cells/mouse) for 60 days induced a statistically significant increase in ALT, AST, LDH, and total bilirubin levels, and increased the number of GFAP-positive astrocytes in the cerebral cortex (p = 0.046) compared with the control group. In contrast, lower doses (50 × 10  3 and 150 × 10  3 cells/mouse) did not cause elevated blood markers or astrogliosis. No significant changes in locomotor or exploratory behaviour were observed in the open field test, and no pathomorphological changes were detected in the brain in any group. Conclusions Chronic retro-orbital administration of GPCs at 500 × 10  3 cells/mouse was associated with signs of inflammation and liver damage, whereas doses of 50 × 10  3 and 150 × 10  3 cells/mouse were safe and optimal. These findings provide important pharmacological parameters for designing preclinical studies using long-term GPC administration in mice.

raw.abstractText: To explore the feasibility of using coal gasification slag (CGS) as a substitute for limestone filler (LF) in asphalt mastic, six representative CGS powders and one commonly used LF were selected. The physicochemical properties of the CGS powders and the rheological properties of the corresponding asphalt mastics were investigated, and an economic evaluation was conducted. Through comparative analysis of the high- and low-temperature rheological properties of the asphalt mastics at a fixed filler-to-binder (F/B) ratio of 1.0 by mass, low-carbon gasification slag generated by the pulverized-coal process (coded as LCPGS) was identified as the preferred raw material, achieving the optimal balance between high- and low-temperature properties. Compared with LF asphalt mastic, LCPGS asphalt mastic (LCPGS-AM) showed a 19.4% higher G*/sinδ at 64 °C, while m/S value at −12 °C was only 2.2% lower. Based on the rheological and fatigue-resistance properties of LCPGS-AMs with different F/B ratios, a suitable F/B range of 30%–40% by volume was determined, which can serve as a reference for asphalt mastic and mixture design. Complete replacement of conventional LF with LCPGS can reduce material cost by approximately 56.3%, yielding significant economic benefits. The preliminary performance and economic analyses indicate that the use of CGS powder as an alternative filler in asphalt mixtures is feasible.

raw.abstractText: Digital logistics can improve visibility, coordination, reliability, and customer interaction, yet technological sophistication alone does not guarantee that firms realize these benefits. This study identifies conditions that are necessary and alternative configurations that are sufficient for high perceived e-logistics effectiveness in Bangladesh’s ready-made garment (RMG) sector. A cross-sectional survey used random respondent selection, 70 professionals were invited and 60 usable questionnaires were returned (85.7%). Necessary Condition Analysis (NCA) and fuzzy set Qualitative Comparative Analysis (fsQCA) were combined. The study specific four-item benefit composite shows strong empirical coherence (Cronbach’s α = 0.936; McDonald’s ω = 0.937). CE-FDH NCA with 10,000 permutations identifies top management awareness as the only condition with both a practically meaningful and statistically supported necessity effect (d = 0.433, p < 0.001). Using frequency ≥ 2, consistency ≥ 0.80, and standard PRI ≥ 0.65, the observed-data complex fsQCA solution identifies two pathways: MGT*~TECH*~INTL*EXT and MGT*SIZE*INTL*EXT, with solution consistency 0.963 and coverage 0.595. A separate low outcome analysis yields different configurations, supporting causal asymmetry. Robustness checks show that management awareness is the most stable cross specification element, while exact pathway structure is sensitive to some coding and case-exclusion choices. The study contributes a transparent, bounded configurational explanation of e-logistics benefit realization in Bangladesh RMG.

raw.abstractText: This study investigates the potential of a development framework for generating personalized light schedules aimed at achieving specific sleep-wake cycle targets. Unlike existing approaches that rely on predefined heuristics or static lighting recommendations, the framework formulates light scheduling as a sequential decision-making problem and employs a reinforcement learning–based deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) algorithm to iteratively modify real-world light exposure patterns toward achieving a desired sleep-wake class. This process is assisted by a convolutional neural network-based sleep-wake classification model trained on ecologically collected data. The circadian impacts of the generated schedules are evaluated using dim light melatonin onset (DLMO) simulations from a validated circadian model. By incorporating melanopic alongside photopic illuminances and embedding industry-oriented constraints, this work explores possibilities of a novel method in generating and modifying light schedules for sleep-wake adjustments using modern approaches, standards and findings.

raw.abstractText: Ca2+ is both the signal that spreads injury information through the endothelium and the trigger for phospholipid scrambling that makes a membrane procoagulant. How a blood vessel can disseminate the first without broadcasting the second is unknown. Here, we combine single-cell laser injury in endothelial monolayers with imaging of intact mesenteric vessels in vitro and intravital Ca2+ imaging in vivo. Injury generated a coherent Ca2+ wavefront that spread rapidly before progressively slowing and terminating at a reproducible boundary 197 ± 7 μm from the wound, engaging 50 ± 8 cells. The first ring of neighboring cells exhibited a distinct response that was prevented by carbenoxolone, whereas propagation beyond this ring required extracellular ATP, purinergic receptor activation, and IP3-dependent Ca2+ release. Wavefront kinematics were consistent with ATP diffusion. In vivo, injury elicited vasoconstriction and bidirectional Ca2+ waves propagating 205 ± 28 μm before terminating. Remarkably, despite widespread Ca2+ elevations, phosphatidylserine (PS) externalization remained confined to the wounded cell in monolayers and intact vessels in vitro. In contrast, ionomycin-induced Ca2+ overload exposed phosphatidylserine in nearly all endothelial cells. These findings reveal an unexpected spatial uncoupling between endothelial Ca2+ signaling and phospholipid scrambling, demonstrating that Ca2+ dependent scramblase activation is subject to additional spatial regulation. The endothelium can therefore propagate injury signals across a broad field of cells while maintaining a highly localized procoagulant membrane response.

raw.abstractText: Volume-regulated anion channels (VRACs) are swelling-activated Cl⁻ channels formed by heteromers of LRRC8 proteins (LRRC8A-E). VRACs mediate regulatory volume decrease by releasing Cl⁻ and organic osmolytes, including taurine. In the brain, taurine functions as both an osmolyte and an inhibitory neuromodulator, acting as an agonist at glycine and GABAA receptors. Here, we used RNAi and genetically modified mice to (i) determine the contribution of LRRC8 subunits to swelling-activated taurine release, and (ii) test whether brain VRACs contribute to systemic osmoregulation. In astrocyte cultures lacking the essential VRAC subunit LRRC8A, swelling-activated [3H]taurine release was reduced by ~90%. Similarly, in vivo brain microdialysis revealed a ≥90% reduction in swelling-activated taurine release in brain-wide LRRC8A knockout mice (bLRRC8A KO). RNAi experiments further confirmed LRRC8D as a key determinant of VRAC-mediated taurine release, with Lrrc8d knockdown reducing swelling activated [3H]taurine efflux by >50%. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of Lrrc8d in the hypothalamus, where astrocytic taurine release is proposed to inhibit magnocellular neurons and suppress arginine vasopressin secretion during hypoosmotic conditions. We therefore tested whether disrupting brain VRACs impairs recovery from systemic hypoosmotic stress. bLRRC8A KO mice and mice with gene trap-mediated LRRC8D depletion were challenged with an intraperitoneal injection of sterile water (7.5% body weight, under anesthesia), and serum osmolality was monitored over time. Unexpectedly, neither model showed impaired recovery from hypoosmotic challenge. Overall, this study identifies LRRC8A/D-containing VRACs as the primary conduit for swelling-activated taurine release in the brain, yet indicates that this pathway is not essential for maintaining systemic fluid-electrolyte homeostasis.

raw.abstractText:
Background

Dopamine neurons in the ventral tegmental area (VTA), a midbrain structure, have been widely implicated in promoting emergence from general anesthesia. However, most studies have focused on anesthetics that primarily target γ-aminobutyric acid type A receptors. Whether these neurons also facilitate emergence from mechanistically diverse drug-induced unconscious states is not known. This study examined the specific contribution of VTA dopamine neurons in restoring arousal after sevoflurane-, dexmedetomidine-, fentanyl-, and ketamine-induced unconsciousness.

Methods

Adult Sprague Dawley rats received viral constructs driving selective expression in tyrosine hydroxylase-positive VTA neurons of either channelrhodopsin or the control protein, yellow fluorescent protein. Accurate targeting in VTA TH:ChR was confirmed by assessing righting in response to photostimulation during continuous sevoflurane inhalation (1.4 to 2.0%). In a randomized block design, the rats were exposed to dexmedetomidine (15 µg/kg IV bolus), fentanyl (50 µg/kg IV bolus), or ketamine (50 mg/kg IV infusion). After loss of the righting reflex, behavioral arousal and frontal electroencephalography activity were recorded with or without photostimulation. The proportion of animals righting during the light-on and light-off conditions was assessed in a mixed-effects Cox regression model, and spectral power differences were quantified with effect size estimates.

Results

Optogenetic stimulation of VTA dopamine neurons during continuous sevoflurane inhalation restored righting in VTA TH:ChR rats, with a median latency of 4.7 min (95% CI, 2.6 to 6.4) after the onset of photostimulation. VTA TH:ChR rats were significantly more likely to right during photostimulation after dexmedetomidine (hazard ratio, 27.7; 95% CI, 2.7 to 287.1; P = 0.0053), and responders showed attenuated spectral power in low frequencies (less than 12 Hz) in VTA TH:ChR . Optogenetic stimulation did not affect behavioral nor neurophysiologic measures of arousal after fentanyl. Finally, optogenetic stimulation in VTA TH:ChR rats modestly delayed emergence from ketamine sedation without altering electroencephalography spectral power.

Conclusions

These data suggest that the role of dopamine VTA neurons in anesthetic emergence is agent specific and likely shaped by distinct and sometimes opposing neural pathways.

raw.abstractText: Benzylisoquinoline alkaloids (BIAs) are a class of structurally diverse secondary metabolites, with over 2,500 identified variants classified into seven major categories based on their core skeletons. These compounds exhibit significant pharmacological activities - including antitumor, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory effects - and serve as important sources of clinical drugs such as morphine, berberine, and magnoflorine. Currently, BIAs are primarily obtained through plant cultivation and extraction. However, factors such as low in-planta content, seasonal constraints, and environmental variability contribute to vulnerabilities in the supply chain. In light of these challenges, microbial biosynthesis using engineered strains (e.g., yeast) has emerged as a promising alternative, though it requires complete elucidation and functional expression of all pathway enzymes. Enhancing BIAs production in crops through transcriptional regulation - targeting key enzymes, transcription factors (such as WRKY, bHLH, and AP2/ERF families), and phytohormone signaling - represents a feasible interim strategy. Advanced approaches, including coexpression of enzyme genes and transcription factors, hold promise for accelerating the development of industrial-scale alkaloid-producing cell factories and crop improvement, thereby enabling sustainable drug supply.

raw.abstractText: There is accumulating evidence that the GLP-1 analog, semaglutide, might effectively curb intake of cocaine via brain dopaminergic functioning, despite limited brain penetrance. However, there is currently no established mechanism elucidating how chronic semaglutide treatment regulates the dopaminergic response to cocaine. Cocaine is a highly addictive substance that produces rewarding effects primarily through antagonism of the dopamine transporter (DAT). Therapeutics for cocaine use disorder (CUD) have long targeted DAT in the hope of reducing cocaine intake. Metabolic hormones such as leptin and insulin have been shown to influence DAT, and for that reason have been explored for the regulation of cocaine reward and behavior. Interestingly, while semaglutide does not penetrate the brain, it does peripherally modulate metabolic hormones that enter the brain. Through fast-scan cyclic voltammetry and behavioral experimentation, we examined the effects of chronic semaglutide treatment on dopamine signaling, cocaine-induced dopamine release, and locomotor sensitivity. We determined that chronic semaglutide inhibits dopaminergic reward induced by cocaine. Surprisingly, semaglutides effects on cocaine reward were blunted in mice fasted overnight, suggesting a mechanistic dependence on metabolic hormones. Semaglutide administration generated significant reductions in fasting blood leptin, as well as enhanced striatal leptin sensitivity compared to vehicle controls. Preceding cocaine exposure, application of leptin to fasted mice restored semaglutides regulation of cocaine. Our results exhibit a potential mechanism for semaglutide-induced cocaine reward inhibition, emphasizing the potential of central leptin signaling as a therapeutic target for CUD.

raw.abstractText: Many widely used nutraceuticals, including curcuminoids, polyphenols, carotenoids, coenzyme Q10 and labile vitamins, reach the systemic circulation poorly after oral intake because of low solubility, gastrointestinal degradation, efflux and presystemic conjugation. Lipid-based nanocarriers have become the leading commercial solution. This narrative review examines liposomes, niosomes, solid lipid nanoparticles, nanostructured lipid carriers, nanoemulsions, micelles and self-emulsifying systems for nutraceutical delivery. It explains the three mechanisms by which lipid excipients raise absorption (mixed-micelle solubilisation, lymphatic transport and modulation of enterocyte handling), compares carrier classes on composition, stability and manufacturability, and examines the conversion of liquid dispersions into stable powders, using spray-dried liposomal vitamin C as a worked example. Human pharmacokinetic studies are tabulated and critically appraised. Reported gains range from about 1.3-fold to more than 180-fold, but this spread reflects study design as much as technology: measurement of total rather than unconjugated analyte, unequal comparator doses, small industry-funded cohorts and few head-to-head comparisons. In the most rigorous equal-dose comparison of eight curcumin formulations, only micellar and cyclodextrin products outperformed native curcumin. The review proposes critical quality attributes for lipid-based ingredients and a minimum reporting standard for future bioavailability trials.

raw.abstractText: Achieving broadband and omnidirectional solar absorption is critical for advancing high-efficiency photovoltaic technologies. Surface engineering via subwavelength arrays offers a robust pathway for enhanced light trapping. Recently, Light Funnel Mixer (LFM) arrays-comprised of inverted subwavelength cones featuring deep subwavelength sidewall decorations-have demonstrated superior absorption potential. This study investigates the influence of the LFM bottom diameter on light-trapping efficiency using Near-field Scanning Optical Microscopy (NSOM). Two complementary characterization modes are employed: the analysis of far-field distributions under near-field excitation and the mapping of near-field distributions under far-field excitation. The optical response of LFM arrays is benchmarked against standard Light Funnel (LF) and Nanopillar (NP) arrays to isolate the impact of the structural decorations. Our results indicate that, unlike LF structures, LFM arrays exhibit a strong performance dependency on the bottom diameter. Specifically, decreasing the bottom diameter leads to a significant reduction in far-field reflection. Simultaneously, the near-field intensity within the LFM arrays increases as the bottom diameter narrows, indicating enhanced optical excitation and the generation of greater lateral momentum components. These findings directly imply a higher probability of photon absorption in optimized LFM geometries. Experimental observations are corroborated by three-dimensional numerical calculations, providing a comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms governing enhanced light-matter interaction in decorated subwavelength architectures. This work underscores the importance of precise geometric tuning in the design of next-generation solar energy harvesters.

raw.abstractText: Problematic social media use has emerged as a significant global public health concern, particularly among university students. This systematic review synthesizes contemporary evidence across diverse geographical contexts to evaluate the relationship between social media addiction and objective sleep quality parameters. Following strict inclusion criteria, ten high-quality empirical studies, systematic reviews, and meta-analyses published between 2023 and 2026—representing populations in Bangladesh, China, India, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia, the United Kingdom, Nigeria, and Brazil—were synthesized. The collective findings across a cumulative sample size of over 40,000 participants demonstrate a robust, negative correlation between excessive digital exposure and sleep duration. Late-night screen time, driven by Fear of Missing Out (FoMo) and digital fatigue, severely alters circadian rhythms and suppresses melatonin secretion, leading to fragmented sleep, daytime sleepiness, and heightened depressive symptoms. While protective behavioral strategies like physical exercise offer a viable mitigation buffer, their efficacy is heavily undermined by extreme digital dependencies. In conclusion, unregulated social media consumption poses an escalating threat to student well-being. Immediate multi-sectoral interventions, digital literacy programs, and campus-based health policies are required to safeguard the physical and psychological health of the higher education workforce.

raw.abstractText:
Background:

High-concentration 7-hydroxymitragynine (7-OH) products have been described by the US Food and Drug Administration as an emerging public health concern, and in August 2026 the Drug Enforcement Administration temporarily placed mitragynine pseudoindoxyl (MP), MGM-15 (dihydro-7-hydroxymitragynine), and MGM-16 in schedule I. Since July, Utah and Tennessee officials have reported overdoses, deaths, and laboratory findings involving tablets labeled as cat's claw (Uncaria tomentosa), an herbal supplement without known opioid activity. Chemical data on such products are scarce, and consumers cannot tell from the label which opioid-active compounds they contain.

Methods:

In a cross-sectional analysis, we purchased 46 chewable or unit-dose products labeled as containing cat's claw from online retailers and 3 gas stations in Mississippi during September 2026. The products represented 17 brands. Methanol extracts were analyzed by ultra-high-performance liquid chromatography with photodiode array detection and compared with a methanol extract of botanically verified U tomentosa bark. Liquid chromatography quadrupole time of flight mass spectrometry identified additional compounds, and compounds were quantified against authentic reference standards. Proportions are reported with exact (Clopper-Pearson) 95% CIs.

Results:

None of the 46 products declared kratom alkaloids or their derivatives, yet all contained at least one component. Mitragynine was quantified in 41 products (89%; 95% CI, 76% to 96%), 7-OH in 35 (76%; 95% CI, 61% to 87%), MGM-15 in 24 (52%; 95% CI, 37% to 67%), and MP in 22 (48%; 95% CI, 33% to 63%). A total of 39 products (85%; 95% CI, 71% to 94%) contained MP or MGM-15, which are temporarily controlled in schedule I. Tianeptine, an antidepressant not approved in the US, was present in five products (11%; 95% CI, 4% to 24%) at 27.9 to 40.2 mg per unit. The 7-OH content ranged from 0.01 to 95.4 mg per unit. Eight products carrying claims such as "NO KRATOM and No 7-OH" or "NO 7-OH" contained mitragynine, 7-OH, and 3-dehydromitragynine.

Conclusions:

Labels gave consumers no reliable guide to exposure. Clinicians evaluating unexplained opioid toxicity after use of a cat's claw product should consider kratom-derived opioids and tianeptine. Regulators may need product testing and label enforcement in addition to scheduling of individual compounds.

raw.abstractText: Objective Preeclampsia continues to be a primary cause of health complications and death for expectant mothers and their unborn children. Early identification of pregnant women at risk, followed by timely preventive interventions, carries clear clinical value. We examined whether the serum uric acid to creatinine ratio (UA/Cr) measured at admission is associated with preeclampsia and whether it adds discriminative value when used in machine learning (ML) models. Methods We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study using the MIMIC-IV database, identifying 4,756 pregnant women with gestational age ≥ 20 weeks; 4,247 were excluded for missing data, leaving 509 for analysis (78 preeclampsia cases, 431 controls). Preeclampsia was identified by ICD-9/10 codes. UA/Cr (uric acid mg/dL ÷ creatinine mg/dL, first admission-day value) entered logistic regression as both a continuous variable and a quartile variable (Q1 as reference), with two adjustment sets: Model 1 adjusted for age, and Model 2 for age, language, and red blood cell count. Restricted cubic splines characterized nonlinearity, and subgroup analyses tested robustness. Six machine learning algorithms—random forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, AdaBoost, and TabPFN—were trained on the training set (n = 355) and validated on the validation set (n = 154). Features were selected by univariate screening, variance inflation factor (VIF) diagnostics, and LASSO.Univariate analysis for screening, VIF diagnostics, and LASSO were utilized to choose features. Result UA/Cr rose with preeclampsia risk and the dose–response curve was approximately linear (nonlinearity P = 0.911): each 1-unit increment was associated with an OR of 1.184 (95% CI 1.061–1.320, P = 0.002). The highest quartile carried an OR of 2.758 versus the lowest quartile (95% CI 1.318–6.128, P = 0.009; trend P = 0.020). AUCs in the validation set ranged from 0.655 to 0.761 (LightGBM the highest), with UA/Cr ranking second in feature importance. The four top-performing models did not differ significantly from one another. Conclusion In this MIMIC-IV cohort of hospitalized pregnant women, a higher admission UA/Cr was associated with preeclampsia, and an ML model built from routine admission data achieved moderate concurrent discrimination. Because of the cross-sectional design, the analysis does not support prospective prediction. Prospective and external validation, alongside head-to-head comparison with absolute uric acid, is required before any clinical use in risk stratification.

Objectives

Hypovitaminosis D is common in children with transfusion-dependent thalassemia (TDT) because of chronic iron overload and endocrine dysfunction. This study assessed baseline vitamin D status, response to supplementation, and factors associated with treatment response and maintenance of sufficiency.

Methods

In this prospective observational study, children aged 1-18 y with TDT underwent assessment of demographic, clinical, biochemical, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D levels. Vitamin D deficiency, insufficiency, and sufficiency were defined as <12 ng/mL, 12-20 ng/mL, and >20 ng/mL, respectively. Children with deficient or insufficient levels received oral vitamin D (60,000 IU weekly for 6 wk) with calcium supplementation. Vitamin D levels were reassessed after 3 mo; non-responders received repeat supplementation, while responders were followed for maintenance of sufficiency.

Results

Among 93 children, 89 (95.7%) had hypovitaminosis D, with a mean baseline vitamin D level of 11.63 ± 5.66 ng/mL. Following supplementation, 60 (67.4%) achieved sufficiency, while 29 (32.6%) remained deficient/insufficient. Of those achieving sufficiency, only 14 (23.3%) maintained adequate levels at 3-mo follow-up, whereas 46 (76.7%) again became deficient/insufficient. Repeat supplementation resulted in sufficiency in 20/29 (69.0%) children. Baseline vitamin D levels showed a significant negative correlation with serum ferritin (ρ = -0.664, p <0.001).

Conclusions

Hypovitaminosis D is highly prevalent in children with TDT and is strongly associated with iron overload. Although supplementation effectively improves vitamin D levels, maintenance of sufficiency after discontinuation remains poor, emphasizing the need for regular monitoring and maintenance supplementation.

The associations between ultrasound-assessed steatosis, liver size, and metabolic abnormalities have previously been studied without considering whether the patients had received treatment. Therefore, we aimed to evaluate hepatic echogenicity grade and liver size in relation to body mass index (BMI) and metabolic markers in newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve MASLD patients.

Materials and methods

In this cross-sectional study, 122 adults with MASLD, as confirmed by a gastroenterologist, were enrolled. Hepatic echogenicity and cranio-caudal liver length were assessed using B-mode ultrasonography. Metabolic parameters, including alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), total cholesterol, triglycerides (TG), total bilirubin, and glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), were analyzed. Kruskal-Wallis and Mann-Whitney U tests were used for group comparisons, while Spearman's correlation and regression models were used to assess associations, including the modifying effect of BMI.

Results

In unadjusted group comparisons, ALT, AST, and HbA1c differed across steatosis grades after Benjamini-Hochberg correction, whereas total cholesterol and triglycerides showed no consistent pattern. Hepatomegaly was associated with higher BMI, ALT, AST, and HbA1c. In adjusted models, grade×BMI interactions were negative for ALT and AST (both P < 0.001), whereas the adjusted grade association between steatosis grade and HbA1c was not significant (P = 0.324). After adjustment for BMI, steatosis grade, age, and sex, liver length remained associated with ALT (β = 0.073, 95% CI 0.046 to 0.100) and AST (β = 0.062, 95% CI 0.033 to 0.092).

Conclusion

In treatment-naïve adults with MASLD, ultrasound-assessed steatosis grade and liver size were associated with selected metabolic and biochemical measures. Negative grade×BMI interactions were observed for ALT and AST, while the adjusted association between steatosis grade and HbA1c was not significant. These findings should be interpreted cautiously in the context of the study's design.

raw.abstractText: Bacterial infections compromise wound healing and represent a growing threat in the era of rising antibiotic resistance. Herein, we developed a multifunctional platform (CN@La@B) that combines bacterial capture, membrane sensitization, visible-light-triggered antibacterial activity, and anti-inflammatory effects. The CN@La@B was prepared by immobilizing dendritic mesoporous lanthanide hydroxide [La(OH)<sub>3</sub>] nanoparticles (La NPs) onto graphite carbon nitride (g-C<sub>3</sub>N<sub>4</sub>) nanosheets to form a topologically structured La(OH)<sub>3</sub>@g-C<sub>3</sub>N<sub>4</sub> (CN@La) heterostructure, followed by loading of the anti-inflammatory agent berberine. The spiky topological La NPs attached to bacterial surfaces, thereby promoting phospholipid dephosphorylation and enhancing membrane permeability. Under visible-light irradiation, electrons from g-C<sub>3</sub>N<sub>4</sub> nanosheets were photoexcited to the conduction band and subsequently transferred to La NPs, enabling electron-hole separation and reactive oxygen species generation to eradicate bacteria. Meanwhile, berberine loaded onto the CN@La@B platform helped regulate the wound immune microenvironment. Collectively, both in vitro and in vivo evaluations demonstrated that the CN@La@B killed bacteria and disrupted biofilms, while also modulating inflammation, speeding up wound closure, and supporting tissue regeneration. These findings suggest that CN@La@B is a promising multifunctional platform for infected wound treatment, based on a "flypaper-mimicked" antibacterial strategy that integrates bacterial capture, membrane sensitization, reactive oxygen species generation, and immunomodulation.

raw.abstractText: Synaptic and circuit dysfunction in the hippocampus is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease, involving disturbances at both excitatory and inhibitory synapses. Adenosine receptors (ARs) regulate hippocampal glutamatergic and GABAergic signaling. Caffeine, a non-selective AR antagonist, has well-established neuroprotective actions. Primary mouse hippocampal cultures were exposed to Aβ<sub>1-42</sub> (1nM) and/or caffeine (0.1, 1, 25, and 50µM) for culture-based assays, whereas acute hippocampal slices were exposed to Aβ<sub>1-42</sub> (100nM) and/or caffeine (25µM) during whole-cell patch-clamp recordings from CA1 pyramidal neurons. In cultures, Aβ increased neuronal death, confirming previous reports, and caffeine co-treatment attenuated this effect. Total GAT-1, A1R and A2AR protein levels were unchanged, whereas Aβ reduced neuronal A1R immunoreactivity; this reduction was not observed with caffeine co-treatment. Radiometric assays identified treatment-associated differences in 1-h <sup>3</sup>H-GABA accumulation and basal <sup>3</sup>H-GABA outflow, including a non-significant trend toward increased accumulation after Aβ exposure and reduced accumulation in the Aβ+caffeine condition. In slices, Aβ flattened the frequency-current relationship and transiently reduced the E/I ratio, whereas these changes were not observed during caffeine co-application; subsequent caffeine exposure restored firing output after 30min of Aβ exposure. raw.abstractText: Background: Sleep deprivation impairs cognitive performance and may alter regional cerebral oxygenation. Nutritional strategies that preserve brain oxygenation could help mitigate these adverse effects. Aim: To compare the acute effects of creatine-guanidinoacetate (GAA), molecular hydrogen inhalation, caffeine, and placebo on regional brain oxygenation and attention-related performance following sleep deprivation.Methods: Twenty-two healthy young adults completed a 24-hour sleep deprivation protocol and were randomly assigned to receive creatine-GAA, molecular hydrogen inhalation, caffeine, or placebo. raw.abstractText: The ability to selectively attend to task-relevant information is central to the performance of a variety of cognitive tasks. Accessible and low-risk pharmacological interventions hold promise with respect to maximizing cognitive performance and augmenting attentional abilities. Participants were sensitive to the trade-off between physical and attentional effort (Experiment 3). However, none of these measures were influenced by caffeine. A beneficial effect of caffeine was observed on the speed of target recognition in Experiment 1 only. Our findings suggest a limited role for the influence of caffeine on the attention system.

raw.abstractText: Choline kinase α (ChoKα) is a biomarker of lung cancer, is overexpressed in 60% of human pulmonary malignancies, and is associated with an aggressive phenotype and poor clinical outcome. Patients with lung cancer who undergo surgery have a recurrence rate of 30 to 50%, indicating a potential need for better tumor detection modalities. In lung cancer cells, JAS239 inhibited phosphocholine production, reduced viability in a dose-dependent manner, and accumulated in the cytoplasm where ChoKα is active. JAS239 had favorable pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics for imaging metastatic lung lesions in mice. In situ and ex vivo fluorescence imaging of primary lung tumors in a canine clinical trial showed distinct tumor identification and margin delineation with a tumor-to-background ratio of 5.0 ± 0.6 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 2.0 ± 0.2 at 0.5 milligram/kilogram. Fluorescence imaging identified a clinically significant event where an occult lesion was found after primary tumor resection. Fluorescence imaging also identified a close surgical margin, which prompted further investigation. Immunohistochemistry for ChoKα showed overexpression in canine lung tumors proportional to tumor fluorescence. Ex vivo human tumor painting demonstrated preferential JAS239 localization with a tumor-to-background ratio of 1.5 ± 0.1 and a contrast-to-variance ratio of 0.9 ± 0.1. These studies establish JAS239 as a safe and effective imaging agent for intraoperative lung tumor detection, warranting further evaluation for human patients with lung cancer.

raw.abstractText: Metabolic network plasticity helps organisms survive change, including dietary fluctuations, transitions between developmental stages and genetic perturbations. To maintain a robust supply of resources under these conditions, metabolic networks must rebalance flux across individual pathways. However, how pathways coordinate their activity to support homeostasis remains poorly understood. Here, we use metabolomics, dietary supplementation, and genetic screening to investigate how the network compensates for the loss of phosphoglycerate dehydrogenase PHDH-1, the rate-limiting enzyme in serine biosynthesis. We find that PHDH-1 dysfunction causes developmental delay and substantially alters the metabolome of C. elegans embryos, but not that of adult animals. Despite these perturbations, Δphdh-1 mutant embryos remain viable through the compensatory activity of enzymes that we identified through a genetic interaction screen. The identified PHDH-1 interactions span the metabolic network and are alleviated by maternal serine supplementation, revealing wide-ranging functional links between serine metabolism and distant pathways. We further demonstrate how the joint action of PHDH-1, the glycine cleavage system and the maternal diet sustains embryonic one-carbon metabolism. Overall, our results reveal how metabolic networks buffer the supply of one-carbon units to compensate for enzyme dysfunction and support robust development.

raw.abstractText: Hepatic abnormalities in non-Fontan heart failure result from congestive hepatopathy and hypoperfusion-related ischemic injury, compounded by neurohormonal activation and systemic inflammation. Assessment of liver disease severity is challenging because standard liver biochemistries, serum fibrosis markers, severity score models, elastography, and imaging modalities have limited diagnostic accuracy in congestive hepatopathy, and hepatic fibrosis is often heterogeneous on histology in this population. Management focuses on optimization of cardiac function through medical therapy or mechanical circulatory support. Although liver biochemical abnormalities frequently improve with restoration of cardiac function, histologic reversibility is variable and not consistently observed. In patients with advanced heart failure needing heart transplantation, histologic cirrhosis and/or fibrosis accompanied by portal hypertension may merit consideration of combined heart-liver transplantation, but correlation between fibrosis and clinical outcomes varies. There remains an unmet need for tests that can reliably assess liver disease severity and predict liver outcomes in non-Fontan congestive hepatopathy.

raw.abstractText: We performed a large-scale genome-wide association study meta-analysis of magnetic resonance imaging-derived liver triglyceride content across 71,488 European-ancestry participants from the UK Biobank, approximately doubling the sample size of previous genome-wide association studies<sup>1</sup>. We identified 60 independent loci, including 31 not previously reported, and estimated the single nucleotide polymorphism-based heritability of liver triglyceride content at 25%. Integrative fine-mapping and gene-prioritization analyses nominated candidate effector genes for 48 loci. Of the 31 newly identified variants, 14 were validated in meta-analyses of clinically diagnosed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (42,163 cases and 1,646,254 controls). People in the highest versus lowest decile of a polygenic risk score for liver triglyceride content had 2.71-fold higher odds of cirrhosis and 7.47-fold higher odds of hepatocellular carcinoma. Plasma proteins associated with the liver triglyceride polygenic risk score were enriched for metabolic remodeling and inflammatory pathways, with liver-enriched protein signatures increasing and visceral adipose signatures decreasing with higher genetic risk. Together, these findings refine the genetic architecture of liver triglyceride content, linking polygenic susceptibility to downstream metabolic and inflammatory pathways and providing insights into the genetic basis of steatotic liver disease.

payload.sourceAbstract: Activity-guided separation of medicinal plants requires linking activity signals and chromatographic resolution in complex matrices. In this study, based on a previously established HPLC-DPPH platform, medium-pressure prefractionation and preparative chromatographic purification were applied for the targeted isolation of free radical scavengers from Saxifraga tangutica (S. tangutica). Medium-pressure prefractionation reduced sample complexity and enriched active fractions, while Click XION chromatography concentrated the target fraction. Subsequent purification on the ReproSil-Pur C18 AQ column resolved this fraction into two baseline-separated active peaks, affording compounds with purities greater than 95%. The isolated compounds were identified as quercetin-3-O-β-D-glucoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside and quercetin-3-O-β-D-galactoside-7-O-β-D-glucoside, a pair of C-4″-epimeric quercetin 3,7-di-O-glycosides. Both compounds exhibited DPPH radical-scavenging activity, with IC<sub>50</sub> values of 68.94 ± 2.77 and 75.59 ± 2.14 μM, respectively. DFT calculations, molecular docking, and ADMET prediction further supported the comparative interpretation of their electronic features, antioxidant-related interaction potential, and predicted pharmacokinetic profiles. Overall, this study achieved the activity guided isolation and activity evaluation of a pair of high-purity C-4″-epimeric flavonol diglycosides from S. tangutica, providing a practical chromatographic strategy for the targeted characterization of structurally similar bioactive constituents from medicinal plants.
